**We get just over a third of the important work done.** This plan finishes about 38% of the work, with the most urgent jobs given the most weight. That's the trade-off for keeping everyone out of the danger zone.

**Other options:** Doing indoor checks during the hot afternoon and outdoor inspections at cooler times gets the same amount of work done and keeps people slightly cooler, so it's worth considering. - Every worker's 90th percentile core temperature must stay below 38.0 °C all shift. Harder work, sun and high WBGT heat people up; 30-min shade rests cool them down.
- Breaks: at most 3 work slots in a row, then a 'rest' slot; at most 2 in a row if any of those slots has WBGT >= 30.0 °C.
- No outdoor tasks during hazards that stop outdoor work. After lightning, outdoor work stays stopped for 30 more minutes.
- Workers who are not acclimatized never do very_heavy tasks when WBGT >= 28.0 °C.
